defaults.permitted_development: A side extension in England can be permitted development under Class A if it stays single storey, does not project in front of the principal elevation and is no more than half the width of the original house. Flats, maisonettes, listed buildings and homes with removed rights do not get the same fallback. In villages and open-edge settings, bulk, roof form and how the addition sits in wider views often matter as much as the headline measurements.

rules.height_rules: For the usual permitted development route, a side extension should remain single storey, stay within a 4m overall height and keep eaves at or below 3m where any part is within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate side-extension depth allowance beyond the wider Class A limits, but the rear projection should stay modest enough that the scheme still reads as a side addition rather than a large rear extension.
rules.boundary_rules: Width and boundary siting are the main practical checks. The extension should stay no more than half the width of the original house, remain behind the principal elevation and avoid creating an overbearing flank wall beside neighbours or a highway. In villages and open-edge settings, bulk, roof form and how the addition sits in wider views often matter as much as the headline measurements.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should stay clearly subordinate to the main house and within the overall height limit. Simple roofs that reduce bulk at the side boundary are usually easiest to justify.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should match or closely resemble the existing house so the side extension reads as part of the original building rather than a bolt-on addition. In villages and open-edge settings, bulk, roof form and how the addition sits in wider views often matter as much as the headline measurements.

rules.permitted_development: In Cheltenham, the Class A test is still single storey, behind the principal elevation and no more than half the width of the original house, but the harder judgment is whether the side wing starts to compete with the main house on a more open plot.

rules.height_rules: In Cheltenham, the 4m overall and 3m eaves limits still apply, but on a more open plot the real question is whether the roof shoulder starts reading as a second wing rather than a modest side addition.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is judged less by a fixed metre rule than by whether the extension remains clearly subsidiary to the original side wall and does not read as an overlarge flank addition.
rules.boundary_rules: In Cheltenham, the boundary issue is usually the length and visibility of the new flank wall from adjoining gardens, lanes or open approaches rather than the dimension on plan by itself.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should stay subordinate to the house and avoid creating a bulky flank mass. On taller side work, matching roof pitch and keeping the addition back from the front are usually critical design points.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials that tie the extension back to the original house, especially on prominent flank walls that are visible from the street. In villages and open-edge settings, bulk, roof form and how the addition sits in wider views often matter as much as the headline measurements.

restrictions.conservation_area: Extensions in a conservation area often need a tighter design and siting assessment, especially on visible elevations or where the scheme would alter roof form, frontage or the rhythm of the street.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually required for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be needed.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can remove the usual householder fallback route in selected streets or heritage areas, so check the property's designation before relying on permitted development.

rules.permitted_development: In Gloucester, Class A only helps if the side extension stays single storey, sits behind the principal elevation and still reads as a narrow side addition rather than plot-wide infill.

rules.height_rules: In Gloucester, the paper limit is still 4m overall with eaves no higher than 3m within 2m of the boundary, but keeping the side roof notably lower than the main house is usually what prevents the flank wall feeling oppressive.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is judged less by a fixed metre rule than by whether the extension remains clearly subsidiary to the original side wall and does not read as an overlarge flank addition.
rules.boundary_rules: In Gloucester, boundary acceptability is usually about whether a real side gap remains and whether the new flank wall affects neighbouring windows, paths, parking courts or small rear gardens.

restrictions.listed_building: The FUL is the application type (for example, FUL is for a full application, HHOLD is for household application, LBC is for listed building consent).
